the proposed modeling approach is an effective tool to integrate a wide variety of hydrogeological, pneumatic, and geochemical field data into a numerical model for the purpose of evaluating flow and transport in complex fractured reservoir systems.
the proposed approach can provide an integrated framework for characterizing flow, transport, and chemical reactions in fractured porous media.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration of hydrologic and pneumatic data with geochemical data can provide a practical approach for characterizing unsaturated percolations and flow patterns in complex fractured rock.

the integrated approach is a useful tool for the site characterization, and that it provides a practical means to improve our understanding of flow and transport processes within the unsaturated fractured tuffs of Yucca mountain, as well as for similar fractured rock environments.

, with the integration of a wide variety of field data and a comprehensive numerical model, it is feasible to characterize flow and transport processes and to evaluate net infiltration fluxes in fractured tuff of the Yucca Mountain area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a more comprehensive understanding of flow and transport processes within fractured reservoirs can be obtained by incorporating a variety of field data into modeling analysis.
the integration of multiple types of data is critical to the success of the modeling analysis of fractured rock, and that the modeling results can provide important constraints to field data.
a comprehensive modeling approach, which integrates a wide variety and a large amount of field data, is essential for the characterization of fractured rock systems.
